notes: Clean design: placeholder names and a dynamic flag are cached at provision (reset on re-provision), and the classification lives in reverseproxy with an updated doc comment. Tests include a solid detection table plus a request-only ServeHTTP test, though that test doesn't verify the POST body reaches the backend intact.

Equivalent to the reference, with a tidy provision-time collector and a relevant doc update; the unit tests on the matcher-set predicate cover all required cases, though the doc text now slightly misstates the transport-error semantics.

Works and even constant-folds string concatenation, with a good test for a truly dynamic name inside a comprehension, but it puts reverse-proxy-specific placeholder knowledge into the generic caddyhttp MatchExpression (`UsesResponsePlaceholders`), a layering smell. It also adds spurious `rp.*` names that never exist at runtime.

Works and folds constant concatenations sensibly, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy-specific placeholder names (plus unneeded rp.* aliases) into the generic caddyhttp MatchExpression, which is a layering smell; tests are thorough.

Closely mirrors the reference: placeholder names and a dynamic flag are cached at provision, and the response-placeholder classification stays in reverseproxy. Behavioral tests cover every case the maintainers listed (shorthand and `ph()`, status, header, latency, upstream host, escaped literal, similar name, dynamic name); only nit is returning the internal slice uncloned.

Collects literal and dynamic placeholder names once at provision time and checks them against the response placeholder list and the header prefix, matching the reference; the end-to-end hit-count tests cover every spec edge case.

Correctly detects static response placeholders (including direct `ph()` calls) and treats non-literal names as dynamic, but it stores the AST and re-walks it on every upstream response in a hot path instead of caching at provision. It also rewrites the LoadBalancing doc and drops the `{rp.is_transport_error}` mention.

Logic is correct, but it stores the AST and re-walks it on every proxied response instead of precomputing at provision, and it drops the is_transport_error mention from the docs; tests are very extensive, including an integration test.

Closest to the reference: zip only renames the member, and squashfs newObjectNative names entries the same way List does. However, squashfs link Open does not clamp a negative offset, so a suffix range larger than the target can panic on the slice.

The zip side matches the reference (suffix applied before root matching, notice names the flag), and the tests cover listing, NewObject, root-at-link, copy and the hostile archive; however, the squashfs link Open does not clamp a negative offset, so a suffix RangeOption larger than the target can panic on the slice.

Works for the main cases, but zip reads every symlink target eagerly while indexing, which adds a remote read per link. Squashfs NewObject/New logic is convoluted, and setting f.file from obj.Remote() likely breaks a root pointing at a nested symlink.

It works for the main cases, but zip eagerly decompresses every symlink at index time, which costs extra range reads on remote archives; squashfs uses convoluted NewObject retry logic, and a New() special case sets f.file from a remote computed before the root changes, which breaks nested symlink roots.

Correct and robust: List/NewObject agree, offsets are clamped, root-at-symlink works, a real `.rclonelink` member wins over a translated link, and the tests include a log-notice check. It does add collision machinery and changes zip Open for all objects beyond what was strictly needed.

Implementation is clean and reference-like for zip, and squashfs lookup agrees with listing, including a deliberate real-file-wins rule for name collisions; tests are thorough (collision, log notice, range/seek past the end, hostile copy), with only a small unrelated offset-clamp and close fix in the zip Open.

Zip appends the suffix after the root filtering, so a root naming `link.rclonelink` finds nothing. Link targets are read eagerly, and squashfs prefers the link over a regular member in NewObject while List shows both. Several test helper comments name the wrong functions.

Zip appends the .rclonelink suffix after root matching, so a root naming `link.rclonelink` is not found while the bare `link` root yields a suffixed object, unlike its own squashfs side; it also reads symlink targets eagerly, lets a symlink take precedence over a real `.rclonelink` member in squashfs NewObject, and leaves mismatched helper comments in the tests.
